title: Stepped Field Survey Station
description: One static field-survey station illustrating the original navigation surveying scene program. A whole published horizontal-baseline rangefinder and complete sloped fictional-map stand occupy a raised observation/notes terrace; two unchanged whole sleeved-marker flags stand apart on the lower field ground. Two finite approach steps separate the raised instrument area from a clear foreground approach and marker area. This is a different spatial task layout from the original small map-and-compass planning pad, not a palette or map-texture swap. The complete four-foot braced rangefinder, both recessed end objectives, central ocular and saddle remain intact; the full old map table, fictional islands and pins remain intact; both flags retain their whole foot/socket/pole/stop/sleeve and blank folded flag. Unit scale, no rotations, identical duplicates are not new variants. Four complete instances of three published models plus four scene-only closed ground/terrace/step solids: one scene and zero new independent models. No optical operation, sighting alignment, ranging, angular measurement, real route/geography, calibration, surveying accuracy, load, stability, stair accessibility or actual route safety is asserted. No people or functioning instruments.
